Subject: [ALERT] fast-path kernel latency spike — region us-west-2

Automated alert: We are observing a 3x increase in request tail latency for fast-path requests routed through the optimized kernel group in us-west-2.  

Summary:
- Spike began at 09:08 PDT; p95 from 120ms -> 410ms, p99 from 320ms -> 1.1s.
- Throughput stable but inflight queue length for fast-path bucket doubled.
- KV cache hit rate dropped ~18% for affected shards.

Immediate notes:
- No instance-level OOMs. GPU utilization at 62% (normal).
- Datadog shows increased retry surface on client side (rate-limiter backoffs).

Attachments: support_log_snippet.txt (tail of router + kernel logs).

Next step recommended (SRE): open an incident bridge, rollback fast-path kernel optimizer or route traffic to warm pool. Seeking owner from Eng/Product to decide customer messaging.

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:46:50 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] fast-path kernel latency spike — region us-west-2

Quick tech TL;DR and proposal: 
- Root signal: KV cache TTL per-shard expired prematurely due to a configuration drift during last week's rollout; the optimized fast-path kernel assumes a high steady-state KV hit rate. When hit-rate drops the kernel's batching heuristics increase in-flight latency dramatically.
- Proposed mitigations (in order of impact/risk):
  A) Route FastRetail traffic to warm pool (low risk) — ETA ~15–20m to update routing policy and confirm. Expected p95 ~150–200ms.
  B) Toggle off fast-path kernel optimizer for affected pool (medium risk) — ETA ~30m, avoids kernel-specific tail but increases average CPU work; expected p95 ~220–320ms.
  C) Model-variant fallback (low-latency-cost tradeoff) — switch FastRetail to a smaller quantized variant that doesn't use the optimizer; ETA ~40–50m, expected p95 ~180–260ms and lower token cost.

I recommend option A immediately and start B as a contingency if A doesn't stabilize p99 after 30m. We'll also push a fix to the TTL drift root-cause (postmortem).

Attachments: heapdump_20270803.tar.gz (no egregious heap growth observed; included partial GC logs).

I'll stand by on bridge for routing action.

-Marissa
VP, Inference Engineering
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: [ALERT] fast-path kernel latency spike — region us-west-2

On behalf of Product/Routing — agreed with Marissa's plan. Going to action routing change now: moving FastRetail to warm pool and enabling temporary per-customer throttles to limit bursty prefixes (we've seen a couple of clients spike prefix-heavy workloads).

Customer message (draft for CS):

We’re seeing an intermittent slowdown affecting a set of requests routed through our fast execution kernel in us-west-2. Our teams are routing your traffic to a warm execution pool and applying temporary safeguards; you should see measurable latency improvement in the next 20 minutes. We will follow up once we validate stability and with a full incident report that includes root cause and remediation timeline.

If you want to proactively reduce error surface, you can temporarily throttle background batch jobs hitting the Gen API; we’ll notify you before we make any further configuration changes.

Apologies for the disruption — we’re on it.

Best,
Karthik (on behalf of Eng/Product)
